correctness.rationale: Independent evaluation fibres have q^(d-2) preimages at degrees d>=2; this yields exact two-point Euler series. Squarefree and Möbius inverse Euler factors combined with Pellet–Stickelberger–Swan parity and character orthogonality prove N+/- exactly. The exceptional q=3 Jacobi terms give a complete four-entry bias table; for q>=5 a primitive-order character has Jacobi modulus sqrt(q), and its Fourier coefficient gives the lower bound; triangle inequality proves the upper bound. A standalone 11,828-polynomial census across GF3,GF5,GF7,GF9 corroborates. No step relies on extrapolating finite checks.

originality.rationale: Comparison of quantifiers shows root multiplicity counts, unconditional discriminant distributions, and two leading-coefficient irreducible counts do not imply two prescribed evaluation squareclass fibres. Seven focused mathematical-record queries plus primary-source inspection did not identify equivalent coverage. Generic polynomial Dirichlet character-L treatments could nevertheless implicitly subsume the result; this is recorded as a residual risk, not dismissed by keyword nonmatches.
residual_risks: Possible implicit coverage by general polynomial Dirichlet L-functions modulo X(X-1) or by unlocated function-field Möbius arithmetic progression theorems.

value.rationale: Exact two-parameter discriminant squareclass fibres refine averaged finite-field discriminant counts, naturally asking how two-point constraints influence parity. The sharp q=3 linear vs every fixed q>=5 exponential growth dichotomy is a structural consequence of character-group order and Jacobi magnitudes, meaningful for all degrees and odd prime powers rather than isolated instances.
